newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end lower on interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end lower on interest rate cut.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower in dull trading on Monday after a lower-than-hoped-for interest rate cut, traders said.
The Bank of Israel announced it was reducing the base short-term interest rate 0.3 percentage point to 15.2 percent.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares lost 1.48 percent, or 2.78 points, to 185.25 on low turnover of 48 million shekels against 37 million on Sunday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index fell 1.58 percent to 195.31.
"Activity was thin throughout day. Investors were expecting a cut of 0.3-0.5 percentage point, but they were still hoping to see a higher cut," said Doron Tzur, head of research at Sahar Securities.
"The fact that the talks with the Palestinians (over Hebron) failed added to the negative mood in the market," Tzur said.

U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross said he would return to Washington on Monday after Israel and the Palestinians failed to agree on a terms for an Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron.
"Investors are taking a wait-and-see attitude. There are no buyers or sellers in the market and every deal moves the market," said Ron Weisberg at I.B.I. Investment House.
"The market was expecting a rate cut of up to 0.5 percentage point, but investors were still hoping for a higher cut. The moderate cut was disppointing," Weisberg said.
The most active share was the First International Bank of Israel, which fell 1.75 percent to 33,921 on volume of 3.1 million shekels. Traders noted that two big transactions were made in the share.

Other active shares included Clal Industries, which closed unchanged at 1,284 on turnover of 3.1 million shekels; and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which lost 2.0 percent to 133,823 on turnover of 2.4 million shekels.
